decisions.reason: A merely topological chart can make the displacement sphere map nonsmooth, outside the smooth-degree and smooth-homotopy interfaces. Requiring a chart in the smooth atlas makes the representative and zero-free radial homotopy smooth; the sphere-cylinder domain is compact, so the homotopy is proper. Reduced degree still covers n=1, with no orientation of M.

F1 incorrectly excludes the empty subcover of the empty cover of X=∅. The comprehension cover used in this proof contains X\S even for X=∅, so the original finiteness argument has an available nonempty subcover; the theorem and choice-free proof route survive. F1 now allows the empty subcover and step 2.1 treats it explicitly before listing a nonempty subcover.

For M=∅, the empty map is the sole lift and its orientation cover is empty, hence connected. The orientable-case remark incorrectly claimed disconnectedness and four lifts without excluding this case. The canonical derivative formula and the nonorientable two-lift statement remain valid: the empty base is orientable. The remark now requires nonempty M for four lifts and explicitly records the unique empty lift.

The block matrix has determinant det(I−Df_x), whereas its orientation comparison is sign det(I−Df_x). The Statement and proof already use the sign correctly. For z↦z³ on S¹, the fixed-point derivative is 3, giving determinant −2 but local sign −1. The title now includes sign; no theorem hypothesis, conclusion, or proof has changed.

The unrestricted generic smooth-perturbation assertion is false. For f_t(z)=z+z²+t conjugate(z), t>0, fixed points are 0 and the three points r=t, exp(3i theta)=−1. The real displacement determinant is 4|z|²−t²: index −1 at 0 and +1 at each other point, totaling 2. These nondegenerate points persist under small C¹ perturbations. Replaced the false two-point claim by f_a(z)=z+z²−a: its two roots z²=a have determinant 4|z|²>0 and index +1. General splitting still preserves the total index, without a point-count assertion.

The algebraic Definition correctly applies to every continuous self-map, including n=0. Its geometric-comparison Remark omitted the smoothness and n≥1 hypotheses of thm-lefschetz-hopf-index-formula and def-global-geometric-lefschetz-number. A point with the identity has isolated fixed points but no geometric number under that interface. Added the exact theorem hypotheses in the Remark; the trace definition, finite-CW comparison, integer-trace lattice argument, AC assumption and continuous-map scope are unchanged.

Nonfatal citation/interface imprecision: F1 Statement gives absolute eigenspaces, as the rejection observes, but F1 Proof 1.1 explicitly constructs inverse cochain maps also for relative pairs; Proof 2.1 averages both cocycles and primitives, and Proof 3.1 applies the two commuting deck projections on the product cover. Thus the mathematical descent is already supported by proved intermediate arguments, not an unsatisfied prerequisite. Step 1.1 now cites those proof steps and explicitly restricts to cochains vanishing over X\Delta, with P=(1−t1*)(1+t2*)/4 proving relative surjectivity and injectivity. Also qualified the two-component parenthesis in step 7.1 for the empty base.

The identity trace calculation is correct for all closed smooth manifolds, including ∅: every zero-space trace and Betti number is zero. Only the concluding geometric caveat fails for empty M. A nonempty positive-dimensional manifold has no isolated points by its Euclidean local charts, while ∅ has no fixed points and the supplied geometric empty sum is 0. Step 2.1 now makes the nonempty hypothesis explicit and gives I(id_∅)=L(id_∅)=chi(∅)=0 for n≥1. Statement and homotopy consequence are unchanged.

ledger_updates.evidence: On R² let f(x,y)=(−y,x), with isolated fixed point 0, and choose the homeomorphic chart h(x,y)=(phi(x),y), where phi(x)=x for x≥0 and 2x for x<0. Then the chart displacement on v(t)=(cos t,sin t) near t=0 is (cos t+sin t,sin t−cos t) for t<0 and (cos t+2sin t,sin t−cos t) for t>0. At t=0 its value is (1,−1), and the two derivatives project onto its perpendicular line as (1,1) and (3/2,3/2). Its normalized sphere map is therefore not differentiable there, outside the cited smooth-degree interface.

downstream_review.affected_use_snippet:
- **Convention.** The condition is written $I-Df_x$, not $Df_x-I$; whether
  $1$ is an eigenvalue of $Df_x$ is insensitive to the order, since
  $\det(I-Df_x)=(-1)^n\det(Df_x-I)$ for an $n$-dimensional $T_xM$ and a
  determinant is nonzero exactly when the endomorphism is invertible. The sign
  matters for the *value* of the local index, not for nondegeneracy; see
  [[def-local-fixed-point-index]] and
  [[thm-index-of-a-nondegenerate-fixed-point]].
- **The two readings agree with graph transversality.** The equivalence of the
  algebraic condition with transversality of the graph of $f$ to the diagonal
  of $M\times M$ at $(x,x)$ is
  [[lem-graph-transversality-is-fixed-point-nondegeneracy]], and it is what
  brings nondegenerate fixed points under the intersection theory of the
  ambient manifold. Neither statement uses an orientation of $M$.

downstream_review.affected_use_snippet:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The polynomial $f(z)=z+z^2$ defines a smooth self-map of the Riemann sphere
$S^2=\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$ whose fixed points are exactly $0$ and $\infty$.
The fixed point $0$ is isolated but **degenerate**: $Df_0=I$ and $I-Df_0=0$ is
not invertible ([[rem-isolated-does-not-imply-nondegenerate]]). Nevertheless its
local index is defined and equals $2$
([[def-local-fixed-point-index]]), and the index of the second fixed point,
$\infty$, is $+1$; the index sum is $I(f)=2+1=3=L(f)$, in agreement with the
Lefschetz–Hopf formula [[thm-lefschetz-hopf-index-formula]] and with the
degree computation $L(f)=1+\deg f=1+2=3$ for a self-map of $S^2$ of degree $2$
([[def-algebraic-lefschetz-number]],
[[cor-homology-of-spheres]]).

downstream_review.affected_use_snippet:
Let $M$ be a closed oriented smooth $n$-manifold, $n\ge1$, let $f:M\to M$ be smooth with
all fixed points nondegenerate, let $\Gamma_f\subseteq M\times M$ be the graph
oriented by the diffeomorphism $x\mapsto(x,f(x))$ onto $M$ and let $\Delta_M$ be
the diagonal oriented by $x\mapsto(x,x)$, with $M\times M$ carrying the product
orientation ([[def-product-orientation]]). Then at each fixed point $x$, for the
ordered pair of factors $(\Gamma_f,\Delta_M)$, the local oriented intersection
sign of [[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]] is
$$\varepsilon_{(\Gamma_f,\Delta_M)}(x)=\operatorname{sign}\det(I-Df_x)=\operatorname{ind}_x(f).$$
Consequently the oriented intersection numbers of
[[def-oriented-intersection-number]] satisfy
$$I(\gamma_f,\Delta_M)=I(\Gamma_f,\Delta_M)=\sum_{x\in\operatorname{Fix}(f)}\operatorname{ind}_x(f)=I(f),$$
the graph map being $\gamma_f(x)=(x,f(x))$
([[prop-the-graph-of-a-smooth-map-is-an-embedded-submanifold]]), and the sum is
finite because $\Gamma_f$ and $\Delta_M$ are closed complementary submanifolds
of the closed oriented $M\times M$. The factor order matters: in the order
$(\Delta_M,\Gamma_f)$ every local sign is multiplied by $(-1)^n$
([[thm-intersection-number-under-factor-interchange]]).

Isolatedness of a fixed point is strictly weaker than nondegeneracy. A fixed point
is nondegenerate when $I-Df_x$ is invertible
([[def-nondegenerate-fixed-point]]), whereas the local fixed point index of
[[def-local-fixed-point-index]] is defined for every isolated fixed point,
including degenerate ones. The equivalence of nondegeneracy with transversality
of the graph to the diagonal is [[lem-graph-transversality-is-fixed-point-nondegeneracy]],
and it is exactly this transversality that fails at a degenerate isolated point.
